paragraphs: Rabbi Chananyah, son of Rabbi Aivu, [Shir HaShirim Rabbah on “How beautiful are your steps.”](https://www.sefaria.org/Shir_HaShirim_Rabbah.7.2.2) Rabbi Yudan bar Aivu, [Berakhot 2:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.2.4.12). Rabbah bar Aivu, [Gittin 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.32a.11). Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi Aivu, [Yevamot 11:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.11.2.6).[^2]

notes.text: These are separate patronymic attestations. The Shir HaShirim verse incipit is retained without adding a modern verse number.

The linked Shir HaShirim Rabbah names Rabbi Chananya son of Rabbi Ivi. The linked Yerushalmi passages name Yudan and Shimon with the patronymic Aivu. The Bavli gives Rabbah bar Aivu and an alternative Rabbah bar Avuha. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=393&lang=en) collects the same four notices under Aivu.
